sections.content:
You know *por más que* and *por mucho que* from B2 Unit 8, *por muy* + adjective + *que* from the same unit, and *por mucha prisa que* + subjunctive from B2 Unit 14. They all say that an amount or a quality makes no difference to the result. New here is the opposite amount, *por poco que* ("however little"), and *por muy* with adverbs.

• *por mucho que* + verb: *Por mucho que insistas, no voy a cambiar de idea.*
• *por poco que* + verb: *Por poco que ahorres, algo te quedará.*
• *por muy* + adjective or adverb + *que*: *Por muy bien que cocine, no quiere abrir un restaurante.* *Muy* never changes.
• *por mucho* or *por poco* + noun + *que*: they agree with the noun: *Por poco dinero que tengas, puedes venir.*

As in B2 Unit 8, the verb is in the subjunctive when the amount is open, and in the indicative when it really happened.

items.spanish: Por poco que ahorres, algo te quedará.
items.english: However little you save, you will have something left.

items.spanish: Por poca gente que venga, la fiesta será un éxito.
items.english: However few people come, the party will be a success.

items.spanish: Por muy bien que cocine, no quiere abrir un restaurante.
items.english: However well he cooks, he does not want to open a restaurant.

items.spanish: Por poco que comió, se sintió mal.
items.english: However little he ate, he felt ill. (It really happened: indicative.)

sections.content: Before a verb, *por mucho que* and *por poco que* do not change. Before a noun, *mucho* and *poco* agree with it: *poca gente*, *pocos problemas*. *Muy* has no endings at all.
